Hi all,

Attaching the V3 comp band draft (Redwood_CompBands_v3.xlsx) and a short summary of requested changes. Key goals: tighten leveling guidance across eng/product/marketing, add geo multipliers for APAC/EU/US, and fold in PayBench benchmarking data.

Can you please:
- Laura: review the leveling descriptions for IC4-IC6 (we still get manager escalation questions there)
- Evelyn: confirm whether headcount approvals for 1H26 require an exception for higher geo multipliers (we have two hires in APAC pipeline)
- Aditya: sanity-check the total comp ranges against the hiring plan / budget spreadsheet

I expect a short sync if there are disagreements on ranges. If anyone wants to loop in Legal/Finance, flag it here.

Thanks Markus — quick pass below.

Summary of my read:
- Leveling: the IC5 description currently mixes senior IC expectations with people-manager outcomes. I recommend splitting the responsibilities into "technical leadership" vs "team leadership" bullets so hiring managers have clearer interview rubric points.
- Ranges: US base + target comp numbers look aligned to market median for IC3-IC5 but IC6 and above are compressed; suggest widening the delta for IC6+ to preserve promotion incentives.
- Geo multipliers: proposed table (in the spreadsheet) is reasonable: US=1.00, EU=0.92, APAC=0.87 (except specific metro adjustments). We should keep an override process for high-cost cities (e.g., Sydney) tied to hiring committee approval.

Small edits in the attached Excel. On headcount: I can approve up to three conversions from contractor->FTE tied to existing budget, but any incremental headcount beyond that needs Evelyn/Finance approval.

If useful, I can host a 30-min review with hiring managers on Friday.

Laura
Senior Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Markus/Laura —

Thanks for sending the draft. Attached is a short market matrix (PayBench_Market_Matrix_2025.xlsx) and a one-page Geo_Benchmarking_Summary.pdf with highlights. High-level takeaways:

- Market medians: Redwood's proposed bands for core US metros sit between 45th-55th percentile for IC3-IC5; IC6+ is roughly at the 40th percentile vs public AI companies.
- Geo adjustments: recommended multipliers broadly align with your spreadsheet, but we propose a slightly lower APAC baseline (0.84) and a city-level add-on approach rather than broad regional buckets.
- Benefits: total comp comparison must include target variable comp and equity; we flagged that Redwood's current equity bands are slightly conservative vs cohort, which impacts total compensation competitiveness for senior hires.

Attachment notes: the Market_Matrix includes sample comparators (OpenBay, Nimbus AI, and three mid-size SaaS firms). We used Q3-2025 survey data.

Next steps we recommend: 1) agree on city-level overrides, 2) run 3 role-specific comps (senior backend eng, product manager, sales director) to validate IC6+ stretch, 3) finalize policy and publish.

Happy to present these findings in your 11/20 review if helpful.

Best,
Anna Ross
Principal Consultant, PayBench Consulting

Markus/Laura —

Thanks for pulling this together. Two operational notes from Finance/Headcount:

1) Headcount approvals: For 1H26, we have budget capacity for 12 net new FTEs in R&D. If we apply a higher geo multiplier for APAC hires (>0.90), we should treat those as costed at the US-equivalent when assessing the hiring plan (i.e., a 0.92 multiplier still consumes near-US budget). Any out-of-band offers (total comp > 115% of band midpoint) will require EVP approval.

2) Hiring committee process: please route any IC6+ offers through the Hiring Compensation Committee; for time-sensitive candidates we can do a rapid approval slot if you provide the PayBench comparisons and target total comp.

I've looped Jordan Smith from TalentHire (recruiting partner) on the thread so they see the updated ranges. Jordan — please hold off on extending any offers above midpoint+10% until we finalize the city overrides.

Evelyn
VP, Finance (Comp & Planning)
Redwood Inference
